# Figures (generated by `scripts/23_figures.py`; numbering follows manuscript v0.2)

Each figure is provided as PNG (300 dpi) and PDF, sized for an 85 mm or 175 mm column. The primary specification throughout is `[dp]`, coverage-weighted, denominator D, unless stated. The 2020 cohort (COVID-19 publication surge) is shown with an open marker and a shaded band. Claims belong in these captions, not in the images.

## Main

- **Figure 1. Study flow.** 18.0 million research articles (2008–2024); 23,920 PubMed-indexed guidelines (19,483 with references) and 7,943 named-body guidelines (7,007 with references); 1,010,117 unique cited papers linked to publication cohorts.
- **Figure 2. Growth of guideline-cited papers against the research literature.** Number of papers first cited by a guideline within 5 years, and number of research articles, by publication cohort (2008–2020), indexed to 2008, log scale. The literature doubles every 14.8 years; papers cited by PubMed-indexed guidelines are roughly flat until the 2020 COVID cohort.
- **Figure 3. Five-year probability of guideline citation, by publication cohort.** Kaplan–Meier cumulative incidence from coverage-weighted life tables, log scale. Labels give the probability as "1 in N" research papers for the 2008 and 2019 cohorts. Named-body, cleaned is a subset of named-body guidelines (Supplement S2).
- **Figure 4. Why guideline-cited papers lag the literature.** (a) Annual log-growth across cohorts 2008–2020 of four factors: coverage-adjusted guidelines, references per guideline, the share of references going to the cohort, and first citations per reference. Their sum equals the growth of guideline-cited papers (P1); guideline capacity is the sum of the first two. The dashed line marks growth of the research literature (4.7%/yr). The decomposition is an accounting identity, not a causal model. (b) Research articles per cohort, indexed to 2008 (log scale): all research (D) and journals that published guideline-cited research in 2008–2012 (established journals; 1.5%/yr), de-duplicated across adjacent years as in the analysis.
- **Figure 5. Robustness.** (a) Cohort trend β in the discrete-time hazard of first citation (H1). (b) Annual growth of guideline-cited papers minus growth of the literature (H2). Point estimates with 95% moving-block bootstrap CIs. β does not depend on the headline age, so it is not shown for the 3-year row. "Censored at 2021" was not pre-specified; it belongs to the pre-specified comparison of the frames in 2022–23. "MEDLINE-only denominator" is a post hoc analysis added after pre-submission review (Supplement S10).

## Supplement

- **Figure S1. Guideline records per year.** The 2022–23 fall in PubMed-indexed guidelines is absent from named-body guidelines, consistent with a change in NLM publication-type tagging.
- **Figure S2. Selected high-volume designs.** Ratio of 3-year cumulative incidence of first guideline citation, selected designs ÷ other research, by cohort (2008–2022), log scale. Cohorts run to 2022 because the window is 3 years.
- **Figure S3. Citation context (G4).** Share of citations that are evidence for a recommendation, selected-design papers against other papers (n = 50 each; Wilson 95% CIs). Intra-rater κ = 0.38.

## Uncertainty (applies to Figures 2 and 3)

Per-cohort sampling intervals are not drawn: each cohort is a census of 0.7–1.3 million papers, and binomial 95% intervals for each point are within ±2.5% of the estimate (about ±3% allowing for coverage weights), smaller than the markers. The uncertainty that matters is in the trends, shown with bootstrap intervals in Figure 5.

Figure 4a and Figure S2 show point estimates of growth rates and ratios; their bootstrap intervals are in Supplement S3–S4 tables where computed, and the pooled S2 ratios are in Supplement S4.
